clue.text: Instrument for tricky operation

blocks.note: first meaning: a violin, in informal speech
second meaning: a swindle or dishonest scheme

explanation.surface: A surgeon picks out the right tool for a delicate procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests surgery alongside 'operation', but one meaning is musical and the other is a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a violin and, informally, a dodgy scam or swindle, both everyday senses.

clue.text: Doesn’t eat with little energy inside – or eats well?

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within the other piece of wordplay

blocks.note: someone who does not eat is going without food
E is the physics symbol for energy; 'little' signals the short form

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether someone is starving or gorging.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer is built from going without food yet means the opposite: E placed inside FASTS gives FEASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To feast is to enjoy a large, lavish meal, which is indeed dining heartily.

clue.text: Official records continued — A to M possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters given could be arranged in some other way

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Records that carried on from A to M, like an encyclopaedia volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A to M' reads like an alphabetical range of files, but its letters join 'continued' as anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentation is the body of formal papers and written evidence kept as an official account.

clue.text: Student less fat around end of September

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps itself about another piece
end of asks for only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: having less fat means being thinner or leaner
the final letter of September

explanation.surface: A student who has slimmed down by the close of September.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying or being taught, such as a pupil or trainee.

clue.text: Soldier in WW2 plane — a good person baling out

indicators.note: baling out is jumping from an aircraft, so these letters leave the plane's name

blocks.note: the Avro Lancaster was a British heavy bomber of the Second World War
taken as written
ST, short for saint, a very good person

explanation.surface: A soldier aboard a wartime bomber as a decent crewman parachutes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and ST from LANCASTER and LANCER remains; the airborne surface makes 'baling out' read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer was a cavalry soldier armed with a lance, so a military man.

clue.text: Story teller has a pose that is strange

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A storyteller striking an odd posture while performing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author credited with the famous fables about animals.

clue.text: Investigative meetings? Act soon with insult going round

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An urgent call to act at inquiries where an insult is circulating.
explanation.definitionFit: Consultations are sessions where advice is sought or matters are looked into with experts.

clue.text: In parts of Yorkshire are daughters nurtured?

blocks.note: the closing pair of letters of Yorkshire
taken as written
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A question about how girls are brought up in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise and look after them as they grow.

clue.text: Praise ace with 250 — ace Izetti is!

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
250 in Roman numerals
A again for ace
the setter speaking of himself says I'M, I am

explanation.surface: A boast from the setter, celebrating the 250th puzzle of a great setter.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Izetti is' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public approval, the same as warm commendation.

clue.text: Charts men constructed as business people

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chart makers at work, compared to people in trade.

clue.text: Shakespearean character, one male in a hundred

explanation.surface: A figure from the plays who is one man in a hundred, rare and special.

clue.text: Form of modern music with true playing bringing great joy

clue.text: Another strange street in Durham’s region

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Leave a musical group performing?

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group of musicians
on, meaning on stage

clue.text: Drink in them — don’t subsequently drive them!

blocks.note: first meaning: bars in a pub where you have a drink
second meaning: closed family cars, called sedans in America

explanation.surface: A road-safety warning: never drink and then drive.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'don't subsequently' turns the two meanings into the familiar drink-driving slogan; in Britain a saloon is both a pub bar and a sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a lounge bar where people drink and a standard enclosed motor car.

clue.text: Tiny amount of time

blocks.note: first meaning, said my-NEWT: extremely small
second meaning, said MIN-it: sixty seconds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, a little while, but splits into two meanings pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt identically, the word is an adjective for very small and a noun for sixty seconds.

clue.text: Boy beside lapping waves maybe in summer?

blocks.note: waves lapping the shore make up the sea
a son is a boy child

explanation.surface: A lad at the water's edge on a sunny holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' places the boy next to the sea, after it in the answer; summer is an example, as 'maybe' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is one of the four seasons of the year, alongside spring, autumn and winter.
